evals.name: blog-routing
evals.prompt: I'm trying out Topcoat (the Rust web framework from tokio-rs). Build me a small blog app in a new cargo project called `blog`: a home page, /posts listing posts with a ?page= query parameter (5 per page), /posts/{id} showing one post and returning a proper 404 when the id doesn't exist, and a form on the post page that POSTs a comment and then redirects back to the post. One shared layout with a nav bar that highlights the current section. Keep data in memory, no database. Make sure it compiles.
evals.expected_output: A cargo project using module routing, module_param!/path_param, #[query_params], href! links, Form + see_other, ok_or_not_found, a #[layout]; cargo check passes.
assertions: cargo check passes on the final project
Routes come from module routing (module_router!) with modules for posts and the post id
The post id is a typed path parameter (module_param!/path_param!) read with path_param
The ?page= value is read through #[query_params]
A missing post returns 404 through a router error (ok_or_not_found or not_found), not a 200 page
The comment handler is a POST route using Form and ends with a 303 see_other redirect
Internal links and the form action use href!, with no hand-written internal path strings
The nav highlights the current section using is_current (or an equivalent request-path check) in a #[layout]

evals.name: live-search-runtime
evals.prompt: Using Topcoat, make a new cargo project `catalog` with a product search page: typing in a search box updates the result list from the server without reloading the page, and each result has a 'favorite' button that calls the server and flips to 'Favorited' in place. Only signed-in users may favorite (fake the sign-in with a cookie named `user`, that's fine for now). Products can be a hardcoded list. Make sure it compiles.
evals.expected_output: A cargo project using signal, $(...) expressions, a #[shard] for results, a #[procedure] for favoriting that authorizes inside the procedure and validates input, keyed loop, router with .discover()/.assets()/.cookies()/.runtime(); cargo check passes.
assertions: cargo check passes on the final project
The search box writes to a signal and the results are a #[shard] fed by a runtime expression
Favoriting is a #[procedure] called from an @click handler
The procedure checks the `user` cookie itself (authorization inside the procedure)
The procedure validates the product id it receives from the browser
The result loop is keyed (#[key]) or items carry stable ids
The router enables discover, assets, cookies and runtime, and the document includes the runtime script
The button flips to 'Favorited' in place via a signal or shard re-render, with no full page reload

evals.name: review-flawed-code
evals.prompt: Can you review this Topcoat page before I merge it? It's src/app/dashboard.rs in our invoicing app. Tell me what's wrong and show the fixed file.
evals.expected_output:
A review that finds the security and correctness problems (unprotected shard/procedure, leaked api_token, hand-written URLs, disabled="false", aria-expanded bool, missing #[key],

, dynamic Tailwind class via format!, unvalidated client input) plus a corrected file.
assertions: Flags that the shard is not protected by the layer and must authorize itself
Flags that the mark_paid procedure lacks authorization and ownership checks
Flags that api_token is captured by a runtime expression and sent to the browser
Flags hand-written internal URLs and replaces them with href!
Flags that disabled="false" still disables the button
Flags that aria-expanded needs "true"/"false" strings, not a bool
Flags the missing #[key] on the loop of stateful components

Flags

as invalid for a void element
Flags the format!-built class and uses class! instead
Flags that `account` and `filter` arrive from the browser and must not be trusted
The fixed dashboard.rs applies the security fixes (auth in shard and procedure, no token capture)
